title: Concordant bilateral grip decline does not establish added prediction of frequent tiredness across two NHANES samples
abstract: A single bilateral concordant-decline interaction was tested beyond conventional grip strength, asymmetry, within-hand variation, separate hand trends and demographics. Source NHANES2011–12 n=4146 showed PSU-grouped CV Brier change +0.00005519. Frozen-specification NHANES2013–14 n=4612 yielded Brier change -0.00000122, joint stratified-PSU bootstrap95% interval[-0.00023513,0.00026261]. Improvement was not established. A parser-error pilot and its correction are disclosed. Existing public-data autonomous AI analysis; no ME/CFS diagnosis or equivalence claim.
